data.situation: On Friday evening, Lin and Jo came into the small room behind the community hall. Two printed messages lay beside an empty mug: “The hall will be closed all next week.” The copies were identical, right down to a spelling mistake. The message was anonymous. Jo turned one sheet over, but there was no name on the back either. Above the desk, the booking calendar still showed activities every afternoon next week. It and the message gave contradictory information. Lin found a photograph attached to the message. It showed a blue note: “Repairs to the hall and kitchen on Monday. It will be closed.” The second sentence was ambiguous. Did “it” mean the hall or the kitchen? Jo put the photograph between the two sheets. Someone might have read the note too quickly. That was a plausible explanation for the message, but neither woman knew what had actually happened. Lin opened the booking record on the desk computer. It revealed afternoon bookings for the hall, with no cancellations. Jo called the caretaker and asked about the photograph instead of guessing which room the note meant. The caretaker checked his work sheet. Both rooms would be closed on Monday from nine until twelve, then open as usual. He sent Jo the corrected notice and confirmed that the afternoon bookings still stood. The claim about a whole week of closure was misinformation. Lin clipped the confirmed notice beside the photograph. The mug stayed empty; they now had a message to put right before people changed their plans.
data.easySummary: Two identical copies repeat an anonymous message about a whole week of closure. A note is ambiguous about which room will close. Lin and Jo check the record and call the caretaker. Only Monday morning is affected; the whole-week message is wrong.
data.easySummaryZh: 两份相同副本重复一条无署名消息，称整周关闭。便条没有说清哪间房关闭。林和乔查记录，再打电话给管理员。实际只影响周一早上，整周关闭的消息不对。

retrievalPrompts.cue: The two printed copies have the same words and mistake, and neither names a writer. Explain why Jo still needs another source.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 两份打印件文字与错误一样，都没有作者姓名。解释乔为什么仍需寻找别的来源。
acceptableAnswers: The copies are identical and the message is anonymous. They are not two independent sources.
checks: 两份副本不视作两份独立证据
无署名不自动等于错误

retrievalPrompts.cue: The note names two rooms, then says “it will be closed”. Explain the problem and why the calendar must be checked.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 便条先提到两间房，随后说“它将关闭”。说明这句话的问题，以及为什么需要核对日历。
acceptableAnswers: The note is ambiguous because “it” could mean either room. The whole-week message and the afternoon calendar are contradictory.
checks: 相同一周的全部关闭与下午开放不能同时成立

retrievalPrompts.cue: A misunderstanding could explain the message. The caretaker has now confirmed closure only on Monday morning. Tell Jo what is possible and what is known.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 误解便条或许能解释消息的出现。管理员现在确认只在周一早上关闭。告诉乔哪些只是可能，哪些已经确定。
acceptableAnswers: A misunderstanding is a plausible explanation. The record reveals afternoon bookings, and the caretaker confirms them. The whole-week claim is misinformation.
checks: 可能的形成原因与确认的安排分开

transferPrompt.cue: Two copies of an unsigned message say the pool is closed all weekend. The manager confirms only Saturday morning is affected. Explain the copies and correct the message without accusing the unknown writer.
transferPrompt.cueZh: 两份无署名消息说游泳池整个周末关闭。经理确认只影响星期六早上。说明副本的情况，再更正消息，不指责不知名作者。
acceptableAnswers: The copies are identical and the message is anonymous. The whole-weekend claim is misinformation: the pool is closed only on Saturday morning.
checks: 新泳池场景与星期六早上
不把匿名与故意欺骗画等号
